cues: The angel drags himself about the house like a stray dying man; Elisenda chases him out with a broom and cries that it is awful living in a hell full of angels.
One winter he has a fever, and they fear he will die.
But he survives, and with the spring sun, stiff new feathers grow, which he hides.
One morning, while Elisenda is cutting onions, a wind from the sea blows in.
She watches his clumsy first attempts, nails ploughing the vegetable patch, and then he gains height.
She sighs with relief, for herself and for him, until he is only an imaginary dot on the horizon of the sea.
